title: Matrix Factorization
description: Collaborative filtering technique decomposing user-item matrices into low-rank representations.
name: Matrix Factorization
summary: Matrix Factorization decomposes a sparse user-item interaction matrix into two lower-rank matrices representing latent user preferences and latent item characteristics, predicting missing interaction values via dot products.
use_when: Building collaborative filtering recommender systems with explicit ratings (e.g. 1-5 stars).
avoid_when: Contextual features (e.g. time of day, device) or content descriptions are critical for recommendations.
pros: Extremely effective at learning latent user preferences from raw behavior logs.
Can scale to millions of users/items using Alternating Least Squares (ALS).
Requires no descriptive metadata about users or items to operate.
cons: Suffers from the cold start problem for new users or items without history.
Cannot incorporate side information (demographics, description tags) natively.
Prone to popularity bias, frequently recommending dominant items.

key_hyperparams.name: n_factors
key_hyperparams.note: The number of latent factors/dimensions. Larger values capture nuances but can overfit.

quick_start:
# Conceptually using SVD from scipy or surprise package
from scipy.sparse.linalg import svds
import numpy as np

R = np.random.rand(10, 10)
U, sigma, Vt = svds(R, k=3)
predictions = np.dot(np.dot(U, np.diag(sigma)), Vt)
